Definition: used in a peculiar sense, the body (probably for the (figuratively) idea of a hard rain)
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says geshem, it means body. The word appears 5 times, and in Daniel it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: geshem matters to me because the body matters to God; He made it, and He will raise it. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace; Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling; Belshazzar's Handwriting on the Wall
